'''Pahari (Poonchi)''' also known as '''Poonchi Pahari''' (Urdu: پونچھی پہاڑی) is a dialect of the [[Indo-Aryan languages|Indo-Aryan]] [[Pahari-Pothwari]] group, spoken primarily in the [[Poonch Division]] of Pakistani-administered [[Azad Kashmir|Kashmir]] and the [[Poonch District, India|Poonch District]] of Indian-administered [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. It is considered part of the [[Lahnda]] (Western Punjabi) dialect continuum, and is closely related to [[Hindko]] and [[Pothohari]].<ref name="Kashmiri2023">{{cite journal |last1=Kashmiri |first1=Naveed Sarwar Shad |last2=Rashid |first2=Haroon Ur |title=Language Dynamics among Pahari Speakers: Trends in Language Use and Shift over Time |journal=Pakistan Languages and Humanities Review |volume=7 |issue=3 |year=2023 |pages=996–1013 |doi=10.47205/plhr.2023(7-III)86 |doi-broken-date=1 July 2025 |url=https://ojs.plhr.org.pk/journal/article/view/830}}</ref><ref name="latifanalysis">{{cite journal |last1=Latif |first1=Iqra |title=The Morphosyntactic Analysis Of Pahari (Kotli Dialect) Azad Jammu And Kashmir |url=https://migrationletters.com/index.php/ml/article/view/11294|journal=Migration Letters|date=2 July 2024 |volume=21 |issue=S12 |pages=186–197 |access-date=20 June 2025|quote=...further classified by Karnai (2007) into four dialects: Muzafarabadi, Mirpuri, ''Poonchi'' and Kotli}}</ref>

== Classification ==
Linguists classify Poonchi Pahari under the Indo-European > Indo-Iranian > Indo-Aryan > Northwestern > Punjabic > Lahnda > Pahari-Pothwari > Punchic branch. Alongside Poonchi, the dialects of Shah-Mansuri, Zaghloli and Zirak-Boli also fall under the ''Punchic'' classification.<ref name="Lothers2010">{{cite book |last1=Lothers |first1=Michael |last2=Lothers |first2=Laura |title=Pahari and Pothwari: A Sociolinguistic Survey |work=SIL Global |url=https://www.sil.org/resources/publications/entry/9130 |publisher=SIL International |year=2010 |pages=1–120}}</ref><ref name="glottolog">{{cite web |title=Dialect: Punchhi |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/punc1239 |website=Glottolog |publisher=Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology |access-date=20 June 2025}}</ref> Poonchi Pahari is mutually intelligible with neighboring Pahari dialects such as the [[Mirpuri dialect]] and [[Kotli District|Kotli]] [[Pahari-Pothwari|Pahari]], which are often grouped locally as part of a singular "Pahari" language.

== Distribution and speakers ==
The dialect is spoken primarily in Pakistani-administered Kashmir's [[Poonch Division]], which comprises the districts of [[Poonch District, Pakistan|Poonch]], [[Bagh District|Bagh]], [[Sudhanoti District|Sudhanoti]], and [[Haveli District|Haveli]]. Additionally, it is also spoken in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir's [[Poonch District, India|Poonch District]].<ref name="Karnai2007">{{cite journal |last=Karnai |first=Muzaffar |title=Karnai, M. (2007). Pahari Aor Urdu: Ik Taqabali Jaiza |journal=National Language Authority |year=2007}}</ref><ref name="latif">{{cite journal |last1=Latif |first1=Iqra |title=The Morphosyntactic Analysis Of Pahari (Kotli Dialect) Azad Jammu And Kashmir |url=https://migrationletters.com/index.php/ml/article/view/11294 |journal=Migration Letters|date=2 July 2024 |volume=21 |issue=S12 |pages=186–197 |access-date=20 June 2025}}</ref><ref name="Kashmiri2023" />

There is also a smaller diaspora of Poonchi and broader [[Pahari-Pothwari|Pahari]] speakers in the United Kingdom, together estimated at over 0.1 million.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Baart |first1=Joan L. G. |title=Sociolinguistic Survey of Northern Pakistan |volume=2: Languages of Northern Areas |publisher=SIL International |url= https://www.sil.org/system/files/reapdata/10/20/69/102069342071601500850856974312702005324/32840_SSNP02.pdf|year=2003}}</ref>

== Phonology and grammar ==
Poonchi Pahari features a rich phonological inventory. One study found 30 consonants, 12 oral vowels, 4 nasalized vowels, and 6 diphthongs in Pahari as spoken in [[Bagh District]], part of the [[Poonch Division]] in Pakistan Administred Kashmir.<ref name="Niazi">{{cite thesis |last=Niazi |first=M. A. |title=The Phonological System of Pahari |publisher=University of Azad Jammu & Kashmir |url= https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362218748|year=2003}}</ref> Stress is non-contrastive and syllable structure resembles that of Punjabi and Hindko.

The language follows the typical [[SOV word order|subject–object–verb]] structure of Indo-Aryan languages. It makes use of postpositions, auxiliary verbs, and aspect-based verb stems.<ref name="Lothers2010" />

== Vocabulary and influence ==
The vocabulary is largely Indo-Aryan in origin, with substantial influence from [[Urdu]], [[Persian language|Persian]], [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]], and [[English language|English]]. Daily speech frequently incorporates Urdu and English terms, especially among younger speakers.<ref name="Kashmiri2023" />

== Script ==
Poonchi Pahari is written informally in the [[Shahmukhi script]], which is the Perso-Arabic script also used for Punjabi and related varieties (including Pahari–Pothwari) in Pakistant Administred Kashmir<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.unicode.org/L2/L2019/19111r-punjabi-lam.pdf|title=Unicode Proposal for ArLaam|last1=Evans|first1=Lorna Priest|last2=Malik|first2=M.G. Abbas|date=1 May 2019|website=Unicode|publisher=Punjabi Parchar|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200421191456/http://www.unicode.org/L2/L2019/19111r-punjabi-lam.pdf|archive-date=21 April 2020|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>, However, being an indo-aryan in origin language, the ancient script has been [[Takri]] as other pahari scripts found in Himachal and Jammu & kashmir region of India, which was lost in time<ref>https://www.peerpanjal.org</ref>.

== Status and language shift ==
Some sociolinguists consider Poonchi Pahari to be a threatened or endangered language, due to its limited presence in education, media, and government.<ref name="Kashmiri2023" /> Younger speakers in Pakistand Administred Kashmir are increasingly shifting toward Urdu and English for economic and social mobility.

Despite this, revitalization efforts are underway. The Government of Kashmir, Pakistan the [[University of Azad Jammu and Kashmir|University of Jammu and Kashmir]], Pakistan and the [[Allama Iqbal Open University]] have supported academic research into the preservation and documentation of the Pahari languages of  [[Azad Kashmir|Kashmir]].<ref name="AJK2023">{{cite web |title=Institute of Languages established at AJK University |url=https://ajku.edu.pk/institutes/institute-of-languages |access-date=20 June 2025}}</ref>
